sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Conditional deep review: BQS 4.58, GQS 5.00 (cash-quality capped) and IAS 5.15. AVP has scaled road EPC rapidly, but revenue growth has not produced operating cash. Base modeled return is 20.3%, dependent on continued financing and replacement orders; ordinary bear loses 90.7% of terminal equity even with conditional rescue. Low historical P/E is not evidence of a safe compounder. This is a financing-sensitive research case, not a buy recommendation. [S1–S5, U1, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026, financial scope is the consolidated group with listed-parent equity and minority claims separated. Audited March balances are actual; April–October cash/debt deployment is a modeled stub, not observed current accounts. NSE close ₹66.80 on 19 October is the latest completed-session observation, not live or executable; 20 October is a market holiday. March 20, 2024 SME listing is supported by annual history and security-master cross-check. October 13 allotment overrides stale master issued-capital data. All four gates are conditional, with reasons in the register; uncertainty is not hidden by a complete score. [S1,S2,U1,M1,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 are audited individually. R 8 follows the supported conditional return spread; D 1 reflects severe impairment; P 5 reflects limited robustness; L 5 reflects lot-aware restricted liquidity. BQS weights are unchanged. GQS is capped at 5 because repeated negative realization is persistent, not merely one evidenced transient working-capital expansion. IAS reuses BQS once and does not add GQS again. All calculations, source links, assumptions and sensitivity cases accompany the scores.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: AVP executes roads, highways and related civil infrastructure, primarily for public customers in Tamil Nadu. Group activities include ready-mix concrete through AVP RMC, blue metals/quarry products through Kanthan, and a wholly owned renewable-solutions company. The parent holds 90% profit interests in each partnership, not 100%; subsidiary cash and profit cannot all be assigned to listed shareholders. Contract execution, certification, retention and government payment timing drive cash realization. The May 23 call stated all FY26 revenue and then-current orders were within Tamil Nadu, so geographic diversification is an ambition, not an established fact. [S1,S5,S7]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Qualification records, owned machinery and integrated material supply help bidding and execution, but public tender competition and concentrated government spending limit durable pricing power. The IPO risk section explicitly identifies reliance on a few large government contracts and policy/payment delays. July 10 unexecuted backlog ₹436.14 crore is about one FY26 sales year; the ₹1,631.42 crore opportunity pipeline is not awarded work. A six-year parent growth record supports execution capability, but does not by itself establish a moat or five-year backlog. [S4,S5,S7]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Parent revenue grew ₹57.9976/63.8885/106.3356/151.0024/272.4524/420.7541 crore in FY21–26, a 48.64% five-year CAGR. Group FY23–26 revenue was ₹114.9808/160.8679/292.8127/441.4411 crore; these are not spliced into the parent series or called organic growth. Parent-attributable group PAT ₹42.106 crore in FY26 increased 27.21%, slower than group sales 50.76%. QIP dilution further reduces historical EPS on today’s shares. Prospectus and later FY23 comparative profit figures differ, so both versions remain labeled in the history table rather than forcing a false seamless series. [S1,S2,S6,S7]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Economic EBIT retaining bank processing/statutory costs is ₹54.3821 crore in FY25 and ₹75.1454 crore in FY26. At 27% tax, incremental NOPAT over ₹140.0764 crore additional invested capital is 10.8%, below a 12–16% hurdle. The all-finance-addback 11.87% proxy is retained as a sensitivity, not the preferred operating metric. Deposits and retention are real project capital: including long-term EMD/security balances raises opening operating WC to ₹315.4791 crore, about 71.47% of sales. Base growth 12%, 16% operating margin and unchanged WC intensity are below reported growth/guidance but still require recurring new awards and financing. [S1,S2,S4,S5]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Three executive directors received ₹3.18 crore in FY26, unchanged; total key-management remuneration/sitting fees was ₹3.4028 crore. Director funding ₹13.4604 crore is included in debt, modeled interest-free while outstanding and separately stressed for repricing/recall. March promoter shares 14,644,993 represented 58.63%; if unchanged, the QIP denominator reduces that to 49.81%, an arithmetic conditional figure, not verified October ownership. Two million warrants at ₹200 received ₹10 crore in September 2025; only ₹30 crore remains on exercise. NCD share security and conditional land substitution are contractual obligations; the actual perfection/release status has not been established. These are monitoring issues, not automatic misconduct findings. [S1,S3,S5,U1]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: Cash weakness predates the latest expansion. Latest comparable FY24/FY25/FY26 CFO is −₹28.5077/−₹15.8310/−₹15.8750 crore, totaling −₹60.2137 crore versus ₹94.5192 crore group PAT. Three-year CFO less fixed capex is −₹152.3318 crore. In FY25–26, additional noncurrent deposit/other-asset uses were ₹43.9993 crore and financing interest ₹30.0524 crore; cash after all these uses was −₹192.3135 crore. The original FY24 CFO contained short-term borrowing, later reclassified; FY26’s FY25 comparative payable movement prints the wrong sign relative to the older statement and balance decrease. The coherent negative CFO totals are retained, not a positive-cash inference. Current taxes, statutory/payroll expenses, employee obligations and legacy tax reserves are allocated exactly once in the opening model. [S1,S2,S6,S7] FY26 ageing puts ₹157.7298 crore of ₹160.0316 crore trade receivables within six months from due date, ₹1.5892 crore at six–twelve months and ₹0.7125 crore at one–two years, with no reported older balance. That supports a recent billing build rather than proof all receivables are stale, but is not confirmation of later cash collection. Retentions ₹18.1712 crore are separately included in other current assets and in model WC. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: ₹66.80 and 29,403,200 post-QIP shares imply ₹196.60 crore equity value and 4.67× FY26 parent-attributable group earnings. The completed dated monthly model pays NCD coupons and exact amortization, term maturities, tax claims, capex and WC, then finances deficits before calculating diluted terminal equity. Bear/base/bull IRRs are-37.9%/20.3%/47.7%. Base exit 6× EV/EBIT is an assumption, not a sector median; the 15% hurdle requires about 5.24× at base operations. A two-way growth/multiple grid, ±3-point hurdle range, cash-tax, credit, tax-offset, capex, minority and warrant sensitivities are included. [S1–S5,U1,M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent loss can arise when certification/payment delays, rising material costs and unavailable credit coincide. Ordinary bear requires rescue equity while most value accrues to debt claims. The no-new-credit base case needs substantial dilution and falls below the 15% return hurdle; complete demand-credit recall is worse. NCD redemptions cluster from November 2027 to August 2028, so a smooth five-year debt amortization assumption would understate near-term refinancing pressure. The contingent GST demand ₹1.1857 crore is described as disputed before the adjudicating authority in the annual report, not a final liability or misconduct finding; full payment is stressed. Counterparty concentration, pledge top-ups and bank guarantees add risks beyond a P/E screen. [S1,S3,S4]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Without rerating or distributions, 5×/10× in five years needs per-share growth 37.97%/58.49%. Base operating growth 12% is nowhere near those rates; leverage can magnify equity outcomes but also destroys equity in bear cases. The bull model’s higher return depends jointly on 20% growth, 18% operating margin, WC improvement and 8× exit, not a single catalyst or a high-probability forecast. Warrants are not assumed to fund growth merely because they exist.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track government-certified billing, retention/receivable ageing, inventory conversion, noncurrent deposit recovery, quarterly bank utilization, actual QIP deployment, director loans, collateral perfection and NCD coupons/redemptions. At ₹5 lakh, conservative 60-day turnover implies 4.78 days at 5% participation ; 2% and 10% give 11.94/2.39 days. All 60 sessions traded, but the official fewer-than-100-PAN and generic SME alerts coexist with that fact; they do not mean missing days. Lot 800 costs ₹53,440 at the observed quote, so 9 lots ₹480,960 or 10 lots ₹534,400 bracket the reference. Short-term ASM Stage I and absent depth/spread evidence prevent an unqualified implementation conclusion. [M1,M_ASM,M_REG1,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Research conclusion: fast-growing but cash-hungry EPC, with weak downside resilience and financing-sensitive apparent cheapness. Conditional quality and attractiveness scores can be compared, but they are not a trade recommendation or assurance of funding. Reconsider the central case if collections fail to normalize, awarded backlog fails to replenish, credit is curtailed, or NCD/pledge obligations become more restrictive. A higher return estimate alone does not repair the severe bear path.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Evidence uses signed prospectus/annuals, the June 16 XBRL reply, issuer call, August NCD terms/rating rationale, October allotment and official NSE market records. FY24 cash reclassification and FY25 comparative sign presentation were visually checked against rendered annual pages and balance changes. Older group earnings versions remain separate. Exact October balance/deployment, current pledge quantities, individual contract recoverability, QIP/NCD expenses and live market depth remain unverified; they are bounded assumptions or monitoring questions, not claims that the model is unfinished. All forward figures are estimates.

limitations: Only fully observed periods included. Missing or pre-listing sessions are not assumed zero.
Turnover participation is indicative, not guaranteed execution; spreads, circuits, lot granularity and trading restrictions remain separate.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Complete conditional factors and explicit gate assessment; no severe governance or unusable-baseline override. High financing and liquidity risk is quantified, not ignored.

valuation.type: Dated actual-opening monthly operating, funding and diluted-equity scenario model
valuation.IAS_status: Conditional on the dated quote and ₹5 lakh reference; forecast financing is explicitly uncommitted.
assumptions: Units are INR crore and crore shares. March 31, 2026 audited balances are actual. April–October 2026 is a seven-month forecast stub, not a verified October balance sheet. Known August NCD and October QIP events are dated within that stub. Investor horizon approximates November 2026–October 2031, five years from the October 19 observed quote; no interim dividend is assumed.

Operating WC ₹315.4791 crore includes inventories, receivables, supplier/site/staff/rental advances, operating current assets and noncurrent EMD/security deposits, less trade payables, statutory/payroll/expense/customer-advance liabilities and current gratuity. Income-tax TDS/TCS asset ₹8.0990 crore and FD ₹0.1032 crore are excluded. MSME interest ₹0.0512 crore is excluded from WC and paid separately. Noncurrent deposits are operating project capital, not surplus cash added again at exit.

Opening gross tax ₹15.1063 crore less income-tax credits ₹8.0990 crore gives ₹7.0073 crore scheduled across the first six stub months; a no-offset sensitivity pays the gross claim. Other government balances ₹1.6188 crore remain operating WC, not assumed available cash. Opening noncurrent employee obligation ₹0.1549 crore and deferred-tax reserve ₹2.9517 crore are deducted once at terminal; neither is also a current operating liability. Legacy deferred-tax release is separately tested, since future 27% PBT cash-tax assumptions do not explicitly model old tax-basis reversals.

Opening ₹234.3930 crore debt comprises term principal ₹67.2791 crore and demand/revolving balances ₹167.1139 crore. Current term maturities ₹24.5106 crore are paid over the first twelve months. Remaining term principal is approximated by ₹20/15/7.7685 crore in the next three years, rather than claiming each individual contract is synchronized. Director funding ₹13.4604 crore is modeled interest-free while outstanding, based on the issuer call; repricing is tested. Existing revolving credit is not falsely amortized over five years.

₹30 crore NCD is issued in August 2026 with assumed ₹0.60 crore issue costs; monthly 12% coupon and ₹7.5 crore redemptions in November 2027, February 2028, May 2028 and August 2028 are explicit. October QIP gross ₹24.9956 crore less assumed ₹0.50 crore costs is credited once with 4,424,000 new shares. Exact expenses were not retrieved; doubling both costs is tested. These funds are not re-credited as IPO money.

Normalized EBIT margins 12/16/18% retain bank processing/guarantee and statutory charges as operating costs rather than adding all finance expense back. FY26 comparable operating EBIT after those charges is ₹75.1454 crore, or 17.02% of sales. Base 16% is not management guidance. Annual revenue is spread evenly within each fiscal year; seasonal collection and execution can require additional intrayear funding.

Base 12% growth is below FY26 group growth 50.76% and below the issuer’s ₹700 crore FY27 aspiration. July dated unexecuted orders ₹436.14 crore cover approximately one historical revenue year, not five years. Base therefore assumes continued competitive replacement awards; pipeline is not revenue. Bear 3% and bull 20% vary execution and WC together. Forecast WC intensity remains about 71.47% in base; bear reaches 80%, bull 65%.

Growth fixed investment is incremental annualized sales divided by 3/4/5 turnover; maintenance capex equals depreciation. Depreciation includes opening ₹7.2716 crore plus growing assets over ten years. Historical capital-creditor advance ₹0.7257 crore reduces new cash investment once. No disclosed capital commitment is invented, but growth cannot occur without modeled reinvestment.

Positive future PBT is taxed at 27%, with 25.17% and 30% sensitivities. No cash loss-tax credits are assumed. Cash floor is 2% of annualized sales. Debt draw/half-month financing interest are solved together. Post-entry total-debt capacity 53% of annualized revenue is an analyst funding rule near March observed debt/revenue 53.1%, not an actual bank covenant or commitment. If capacity is exhausted, conditional equity is issued at half the observed quote, with full share dilution. No-new-credit and complete revolving-call cases are shown.

Before the October share-count observation, modeled cash deficits are labeled unverified bridge debt rather than inventing unreported equity issuance. Base needs ₹22.8660 crore cumulative stub bridge draws, with October forecast debt ₹272.9611 crore and cash ₹51.0959 crore. These are estimates, not discovered October balances. A ₹20 crore worse pre-entry deployment sensitivity tests this uncertainty. Failure to secure required funding means project cuts or distress, not a guaranteed rescue.

Terminal EV uses annualized operating EBIT times 4/6/8; these are analyst assumptions, not peer quote multiples. Subtract all bank/NCD debt and legacy claims, add only surplus cash above the operating floor, then allocate minority equity using FY26 profit-share proxy 0.7367% before dividing by diluted listed shares. This is a small-subsidiary approximation, not a precise subsidiary valuation ; 2% minority value is tested. RMC and Kanthan each have 10% external profit interests; renewable subsidiary is wholly owned.

₹10 crore historic warrant subscriptions are already in March balances. No automatic exercise is assumed for two million ₹200 warrants against a ₹66.80 quote. Full exercise adds only the remaining ₹30 crore and 0.20 crore shares, not ₹40 crore; this is an alternative, not a financing promise. No dividends are counted while retained cash remains in terminal equity.

Returns are before personal taxes and execution costs. A 5% higher entry and 5% lower realized exit sensitivity is shown; lot, circuit, spread and market-depth constraints can be more severe. No scenario probabilities are required or assigned.

reverse_expectations.interpretation: Entry-price thresholds are assumption-dependent, not observable fair value; rescue share issuance can change at a different entry price.

GOV.reason: Related director remuneration is unchanged at ₹3.18 crore, but director funding rose and collateral completion is unverified; no proven severe governance failure.

MOAT.reason: Execution credentials and regional experience help qualification; competitive bids and government concentration limit pricing power.

REV.reason: Parent revenue FY21–26 grows from ₹57.9976 crore to ₹420.7541 crore (48.64% CAGR); FY24–26 group CAGR 65.65%. The starting high-growth band is limited to 8 at Medium confidence because contract/perimeter growth is not verified organic repeatable demand.

DUR.reason: Awarded order book ₹436.14 crore provides work visibility; pipeline not contracted and working capital/funding constrains execution.

CAP.reason: Economic incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is 10.8% at 27% tax, below 12–16% hurdle; bank fees/statutory charges stay operating. Even the original all-finance-addback proxy 11.87% is not strong compounding.

CASH.reason: FY24–26 reported CFO totals −₹60.2137 crore versus ₹94.5192 crore group PAT. Fixed capex and project deposits require additional cash. Repeated poor realization, not one transient build, triggers GQS cap 5.

BAL.reason: Book debt ₹234.393 crore versus cash ₹1.77 crore and DSCR1.01; QIP/NCD improve access but bring dilution, amortization and pledge conditions.

EXEC.reason: Revenue and order execution grew substantially; collection, financing and margin conversion lagged.

EARN.reason: Parent PAT rose 27.21% with operating scale; slower than sales, increasing interest and QIP dilution constrain per-share quality.

R.reason: Central conditional IRR 20.33% versus 15% hurdle gives a 5.33 percentage-point spread. Credit access and replacement awards are assumptions; no-new-credit sensitivity falls below the hurdle.

D.reason: Ordinary bear terminal equity loss 90.7% despite modeled rescue equity ₹12.21 crore. Severe stress can wipe out common equity; adequate funding is not committed.

P.reason: At central operations, a 15% hurdle needs approximately 5.24× exit EV/EBIT versus 6× modeled. Entry is not priced for heroic revenue growth, but funding and exit-multiple sensitivity leave limited robustness.

L.reason: 60/60 observed sessions. Conservative60-day median ₹20.9354 lakh gives 4.78 days at 5%,11.94 days at 2% and2.39 days at 10% for ₹5 lakh. Starting L 7 is reduced to 5 for Stage I short-term ASM, fewer-than100-PAN alert, 800-share lot and unverified spread/depth. Not a claim of guaranteed exit.

gates.reason: Related financing, partnership ownership and promoter-share security require scrutiny. Audited disclosures and primary financing terms do not establish severe diversion or minority abuse; unverified collateral perfection is not called an actual default.

FY26 audited core totals and opening notes reconcile sufficiently for a conditional model. June 16 reply corrects H1/H2 XBRL substitution. Historical cash classifications and a FY25 comparative payable-sign display error are separately bridged using older statements and balance movements, not treated as positive cash conversion.

Three negative-CFO years, debt and DSCR1.01 leave narrow resilience. Dated QIP/NCD are real, but prospective credit and rescue equity are uncommitted. Base can be financed under stated assumptions; severe and no-credit paths demonstrate dilution/impairment. No reviewed source establishes a current payment default.

SM series is eligible and trades on all60 observed sessions. Lot 800, Stage I short-term ASM and fewer-than100-PAN alert constrain execution. Price-discovery status6 is not suspension. Current spread/depth still must be checked before any implementation.
